decisions.statement: A check is handed the whole change.
A check decides for itself what work the change warrants.
A check takes and gives paths under the root the check was given.
A check states each phase the check runs on.
Audit is a phase like the other phases.
A check states whether the check runs there.
A check running on no phase has landed and does not yet judge.
That landing is how a check states its rule before that check binds anyone.
A check the change turns on does not judge the change turning that check on.
The change phase judges only the paths a change has.
A check runs at change before the tree's violation count reaches zero.
Running at change has the count from rising while the rest stay fixed.
A file still with a violation is refused at change the next time that file is touched.
That refusal is the ratchet working rather than the check misfiring.
A mortal page is outside that ratchet.
A check reads any path by name.
A check reads the checkout through the overlay for the paths that check cannot name.
A check listing a folder lists it through the overlay, with the change's edits laid over.
A path the change writes is among the files a check lists.
A path the change takes away is left out of the files a check lists.
A check reads the tree through the overlay, which reads it through the module that reads trees.
Every check listing a folder lists it through the overlay.
The overlay's listing is reached from the shadow a check is handed.
A check reaches every path in the checkout through the shadow that check is handed.
A reach past that shadow answers from the tree git left rather than the tree the change leaves.
A path the change writes is missing from a reach made past the shadow.
A path the change takes away is still answered by a reach made past the shadow.
The shadow's listing, its holding and its page reading are the reaches a check may make.
An audit reads the checkout to make the change an overlay is laid over.
A check's decision is handed the shadow wherever that decision lists.

definition: a module run over a change to judge whether it may land

directives.name: Alan Approves Checks
directives.act: Add a check to akasha only where Alan has approved that check.
directives.warrant: A check binds every writer on every change, and a wrong one costs more than what it guards.
aids: Approving the initiative is not approving a check.
A check replacing an old one still needs approval.
Widening what an approved check reaches needs none.
How an approved check reads needs none.

directives.name: Change Reach
directives.act: Limit what a check measures to what the provisional change could invalidate.
directives.warrant: An audit pays for its reach once a run; a check pays on every change, by every author.
aids: Never scope a check to what the diff touched.
Reach the whole repo where a change can break it.

directives.name: Dispatch Reach
directives.act: Run a check on every file class a violation it judges can arrive in.
directives.warrant: A check the breaking change never runs is clean on the very commit it exists for.
aids: Never dispatch from the files the check reads.
Run it on a file removed, not just one written.

directives.name: Derived Reach
directives.act: Derive a check's reach wherever a new member can arrive, never from a list in the check.
directives.warrant: The member arriving after the list was written is the one the check exists to catch.
aids: A list moved out of the check is still a list.
Never take a big count for a whole reach.
